premortem:

      accepts it without de-duplicating against the orphan's later correct return;

  novel_findings_count: 5

  deep_dives:
    - novelty: >
        Context-window eviction is not a "context not preserved" failure (user named
        that). It is a SILENT continuation failure: the run does not stop, does not
        error, and does not signal. The harness believes it is running correctly while
        reasoning from an amputated framing. This is structurally different from a
        detectable context-loss and is the dominant risk on runs >4h.
      failure_story: >
        Hour 1–3: sim gates strict, receipts accumulate, harness state coherent.
        Hour 4: context compaction fires; the compacted summary drops the active
        probe family M, the canonical registry row pointer, and the PARTIAL-chain
        accumulator. Hour 5: a new child worker spawns with a task card derived from
        the compacted summary; the task card references a lego row that was already
        gated-failed in hour 2 but that fact is not in the compacted summary; the
        child runs the lego anyway and returns a receipt; the controller admits it
        as novel progress. Hour 8: the coupling program claims FULL based on receipts
        half of which condition on evicted-and-forgotten gate failures. The run
        ends with a false-canonical coupling.
      hidden_assumption: >
        The harness assumes compacted context preserves all load-bearing gate state.
        It does not. The compaction heuristic optimizes for narrative coherence, not
        constraint-admissibility state. Gate state is exactly the kind of dense
        structured content compaction strips in favor of readable prose.
      early_warning_signs:
        - "Child task card references a lego row that was worked in hour 1–3 without citing the prior receipt."
        - "A probe family M is named in a child receipt that differs from the M named in the first-hour task cards."
        - "The controller's loop counter and the receipt count diverge (e.g., loop 17 but only 11 distinct receipts in the run)."
        - "A gate that returned blocked earlier in the run appears as not-yet-run in a later task card."
      prevention: >
        Implement a harness-state canary: at loop start, re-read a fixed anchor file
        (e.g., the canonical registry row pointer and the current gate-status table)
        and hash it; compare to the hash stored in the first-turn task card; if hashes
        differ, halt and emit a CONTEXT_EVICTION_DETECTED signal before any child
        spawns. Never continue a loop iteration without a matching hash.

    - novelty: >
        PARTIAL-escalation gate-bypass is not "gates may not remain strict."
        Strict gates fail loudly (return blocked, stop the chain). The PARTIAL
        bypass is gates that appear strict but silently accumulate phantom progress
        through a chain of conditionally-accepted PARTIAL receipts, none of which
        individually triggers a block.
      failure_story: >
        Worker A returns status "partial" — three of five acceptance criteria met.
        Controller notes it is partial but records the three met criteria as progress.
        Worker B's task card is conditioned on A's met criteria only, not on A's
        unmet criteria. Worker B returns "accepted." Controller marks the work unit
        as advancing. Worker C is now scoped as if A fully passed. After four such
        iterations the coupling program has a chain of four ACCEPTED receipts all
        of which depend on a single PARTIAL that never formally closed. The gate
        appears passed; the unmet criteria from A are orphaned.
      hidden_assumption: >
        The harness assumes PARTIAL receipts are held as blocked until all criteria
        close. In practice, conditional task card scoping means downstream workers
        can make a PARTIAL effectively disappear from the dependency graph once
        their own receipt is ACCEPTED.
      early_warning_signs:
        - "A work-unit has at least one PARTIAL receipt in its ancestry that has never been superseded by an ACCEPTED receipt."
        - "Downstream task cards cite only the met-criteria portion of an upstream PARTIAL without naming the unmet criteria."
        - "The gap between the number of spawned workers and the number of formally ACCEPTED receipts grows across the run."
      prevention: >
        Add a PARTIAL ledger: every PARTIAL receipt is logged with its unmet criteria
        as open items; a work-unit cannot advance past its gate until every open item
        in its ancestry chain is either ACCEPTED or explicitly KILLED with a named
        reason. The controller checks the PARTIAL ledger before each loop iteration
        advance.

    - novelty: >
        Route-truth self-certification is not any of the user-named issues. It is
        a structural epistemic loop: the audit mechanism that is supposed to catch
        harness drift is itself running inside the drifted harness, so it certifies
        the drift as valid.
      failure_story: >
        After context eviction (deep dive 1), the route-truth check child spawns.
        Its task card is generated from the evicted harness framing. It reads the
        same compacted context the controller reads. It checks whether the current
        route matches the original route-truth document — but the original route-truth
        document pointer was in the evicted state. It falls back to the last-known
        route-truth in the compacted summary, which is itself the evicted version.
        The child returns CLEAN. The controller advances. The audit has certified
        the corruption.
      hidden_assumption: >
        Route-truth checks assume they have access to the original authoritative
        route-truth document, not just a compacted narrative summary of it. On long
        runs, the original pointer is in evicted context; the check silently falls
        back to the compacted version.
      early_warning_signs:
        - "Route-truth check receipt does not cite an explicit file path for the authoritative route-truth document."
        - "The route-truth receipt cites a document that was last read in hour 1 but is not re-read in the current loop."
        - "The route-truth check returns CLEAN on a turn where the active probe family M changed without a gate event."
      prevention: >
        Require every route-truth check to re-read the authoritative document from
        disk (not from compacted context) and cite the file path and a hash of the
        content in its receipt. A route-truth receipt that does not include a fresh
        file-read citation is invalid and must be treated as status blocked.

    - novelty: >
        Async child orphan on harness restart exposes a race condition that none
        of the user-named issues anticipate. It is a duplicate-receipt admission
        failure, not a gate-strictness or context-preservation failure.
      failure_story: >
        The harness crashes at hour 6. On restart, the controller re-reads state
        and re-spawns a worker for work-unit WU-14. The pre-crash WU-14 worker
        was not killed; it completes 90 seconds after restart and returns a receipt.
        The post-restart WU-14 worker also completes and returns a different receipt.
        Both receipts are for the same work-unit fingerprint. The controller receives
        the orphan's receipt first (it was closer to completion). The orphan receipt
        contains a fabricated result because it was running against pre-crash
        (now-evicted) context. The controller admits it. The post-restart receipt
        arrives 4 minutes later; the controller sees WU-14 already ACCEPTED and
        discards the correct receipt.
      hidden_assumption: >
        The harness assumes that on restart, all prior workers are dead. In Claude
        Code's async agent model, background agents may outlive a harness restart
        and return receipts into the post-restart context.
      early_warning_signs:
        - "Two receipts share the same work_unit_fingerprint with different timestamps and different conclusions."
        - "A work-unit is marked ACCEPTED before the post-restart worker returns, despite the restart occurring after the unit was spawned."
        - "A receipt cites task card fields that reference pre-restart state (e.g., gate status or registry row that changed at restart)."
      prevention: >
        On harness start (including restart), emit a session-epoch token (a UUID
        or timestamp). Every child task card must include this token. On receipt
        admission, reject any receipt whose session-epoch token does not match the
        current harness epoch. Pre-crash orphan receipts will carry the old epoch
        and be automatically rejected without the controller needing to detect the
        duplicate fingerprint.
